newsitem.title: USA: CNG holders vote to repeal rights plan.
newsitem.headline: CNG holders vote to repeal rights plan.

text.p: Consolidated Natural Gas Co shareholders on Tuesday approved a motion asking the company's board of directors to repeal a shareholder rights plan adopted two years ago.
The proxy resolution, one of three shareholder proposals considered at the Pittsburgh-based company's annual meeting here, will be taken up by a board committee, CNG Chairman George Davidson said.
"It's non-binding, but we'll take it up with the governance committee," he told Reuters after the meeting adjourned.
The company said it adopted the rights plan in 1995 to protect shareholder rights in the event of a hostile takeover.
Shareholders said the "poison pill" would discourage a possible takeover and entrench management.
"The let-them-eat-cake attitude needs to stop here today," said George Rittenhouse, a CNG union officer who backed the shareholder resolutions.
The CNG board will mull dropping the takeover defense at a time when deregulation is expected to fuel mergers and a consolidation of the domestic electric and gas industries.
Shareholders rejected separate proposals to stop granting stock options to management and directors, and to require shareholder approval of all bonuses over $30,000 a year.
